extracted.intended_audience: general public and physicians seeking home-medical guidance
extracted.subtask_short: home medical guide: malaria & yellow fever
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook-style guidance on the cause, detection, prevention, and treatment of malaria and yellow fever for lay readers and physicians working in home or field settings. Includes diagnostic signs, lifecycle notes, public-health prevention measures, and detailed therapeutic regimens (especially quinine-based) and supportive care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essentials for existence of malaria in a region
rubrics_metrics.description: Two essentials are requisite for the existence of malaria in a region: the presence of the particular mosquito, and the actual infection of the mosquito with the malarial parasite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies that control efforts must target mosquito presence and infection; both conditions must be met for local transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Anopheles vs Culex mosquitoes
rubrics_metrics.description: The kind of mosquito acting as host to the malarial parasite is the genus Anopheles... The Anopheles can usually be distinguished from the [Culex] by its mottled wings, and, when on a wall or ceiling, it sits with the body protruding at an angle of 45 deg. from the surface, with its hind legs hanging down or drawn against the wall. In the case of the Culex, the body is held parallel with the wall, the wings are usually not mottled, and the hind legs are carried up over the back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical field identification guidance for recognizing likely malaria vectors; useful for surveillance and targeting control measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifecycle timing and relation to clinical attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: The parasite enters the red-blood cell of man, and there grows, undergoes changes, and, after a variable time, multiplies by dividing into a number of still smaller bodies... It is at that stage ... when it multiplies by dividing that the chills and fever in malaria appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why fevers are periodic and vary by parasite species (e.g., 48-hour cycle gives attacks every other day; some forms cause attacks every third day or irregular intervals). Important for diagnosis, timing of prophylactic/therapeutic quinine, and understanding relapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mosquito sexual stage and transmission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a healthy mosquito bites a malarial patient, the parasite enters the body of the mosquito... entering the stomach wall of the mosquito, gives birth in the course of a week to innumerable small bodies... These find their way into the salivary glands ... and escape, when the mosquito bites a human being, into the blood of the latter and give him malaria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that sexual reproduction occurs in the mosquito and that a development period in the mosquito is required before it becomes infective — a key epidemiologic point for control and timing of outbreak spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symptoms and prodrome of malarial attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain symptoms give warning of an attack, as headache, lassitude, yawning, restlessness, discomfort in the region of the stomach, and nausea or vomiting. The attack begins with a chilliness... then as it passes away the face becomes flushed and the skin hot... The fever lasts during three or four hours, in most cases, and gradually declines... Such attacks more commonly occur every day, every other day, or after intermissions of two days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes typical prodrome, chill–fever–sweat sequence, variations in children (e.g., convulsions, absence of chills), and typical duration and periodicity — useful diagnostic criteria and for distinguishing malaria from other febrile illnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and severity distinctions of malaria
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregular and severe form--Chronic Malaria; Remittent Form (unfortunately termed 'bilious'); Pernicious Malaria; Black Water Fever; Chagres Fever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each named form is described with characteristic features (e.g., chronic: sallow complexion, splenic enlargement; remittent: continuous fever resembling typhoid; pernicious: stupor, convulsions, possible collapse; black water: hemoglobinuria). Use these distinctions for prognosis and tailoring therapy; note geographic and severity variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitive detection of malaria
rubrics_metrics.description: To the well-educated physician is now open an exact method of determining the existence of malaria, and of distinguishing it from all similar diseases, by the examination of the patient's blood for the malarial parasite--its presence or absence deciding the presence or absence of the disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blood examination (microscopy) is the gold-standard diagnostic test. For laypersons, intermittency of fevers and a therapeutic trial of quinine can be suggestive; failure of proper quinine to stop symptoms usually indicates a non-malarial cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention (malaria): mosquito engineering and personal protection
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mosquito engineering" consists in destroying the abodes of mosquitoes (marshes, ponds, and pools) by drainage and filling, also in the application of petroleum on their surface to destroy the immature mosquitoes... Open water barrels and water tanks prove a fruitful breeding place... The protection of the person from mosquito bites is obtained by proper screening of habitations and the avoidance of unscreened open air, at or after nightfall... Persons entering a malarial region should take from two to three grains of quinine three times a day to kill any malarial parasites which may invade their blood, and should screen doors and windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines environmental control (drainage, oiling, elimination of breeding sites, screening) with chemoprophylaxis (quinine dosing) and personal protective measures. Also advises prolonged treatment/renewal after recovery to prevent relapse and notes communal risk posed by infected persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: General treatment principle for malaria (quinine-centered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The treatment of malaria practically means the use of quinine given in the proper way and in the proper form and dose. Despite popular prejudices against it, quinine is capable of little harm, unless used in large doses for months, and no other remedy has yet succeeded in rivaling it in any way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quinine is primary therapy; attention to formulation, dose, and absorption is emphasized. Pills/tablets discouraged if they may pass undissolved; prefer solution, starch wafers, or gelatin capsules. Beware adulterated quinine; obtain from reliable sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quinine administration: forms and special methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither pills nor tablets of quinine are suitable, as they sometimes pass through the bowels undissolved. The drug should be taken dissolved in water, or... in starch wafers or gelatin capsules. When the drug is vomited it may be given (in double the dose) dissolved in half a pint of water, as an injection into the bowels, three times daily. Infants... ointment (containing thirty grains of quinine sulphate mixed with an ounce and a half of lard) rubbed into the skin... Children under the age of two can be best treated by quinine made into suppositories... two grains each--one being introduced into the bowel, night and morning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides practical administration routes when oral delivery fails (rectal administration) and pediatric preparations (topical ointment, suppositories) with explicit formulations and dosing approaches for infants and very young children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of quinine relative to paroxysm
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of quinine is greatest during the time of birth of a new generation of young parasites in the blood, which corresponds with the time of the malarial attack. But in order that the quinine shall have time to permeate the blood, it must be given two to four hours before the expected chill, and then will probably prevent the next attack but one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrating quinine 2–4 hours before expected chill maximizes preventive effect; informs prophylactic scheduling around periodic fevers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific quinine dosing regimens for cure and severe cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A dose of ten grains of quinine sulphate taken three times daily for the first three days of treatment; then a dose of three grains, three times daily for two weeks; and finally two grains, three times daily for the rest of the month of treatment will, in many cases, complete a cure... In the severe forms of remittent and pernicious types of malaria it may be necessary... to take as much as thirty grains of quinine every three days or so to cut short the attack. If the digestion may be so poor that absorption... does not occur, the use of quinine in the form of the bisulphate in thirty-grain doses, with five grains of tartaric acid, will in some cases prove effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives stepwise curative regimen and alternative regimens for severe disease or poor absorption; emphasizes monitoring for quinine toxicity (ringing in the ears) and alternative formulations to improve absorption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjuvant and symptomatic treatments for malaria
rubrics_metrics.description: During an attack of malaria the discomfort of the chill and fever may be relieved to considerable extent by thirty grains of sodium bromide (adult dose) in water. Hot drinks and hot-water bottles with warm covering may be used during the chill, while cold sponging of the whole naked body will afford comfort during the hot stage... If the quinine cause much ringing in the ears and deafness, it will be found that sodium bromide taken with the quinine (in twice the dose) dissolved in water, will correct this trouble. If the patient is constipated... a few one-quarter grain doses of calomel... followed... by a dose of Epsom salts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists supportive measures for symptom relief and treatment of side effects/complications (e.g., sodium bromide for discomfort and tinnitus, cathartics for constipation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronic malaria regimen
rubrics_metrics.description: Chronic malaria is best treated with small doses of quinine, together with arsenic and iron. A capsule containing two grains of quinine sulphate, one-thirtieth grain of arsenious acid, and two grains of reduced iron should be taken three times daily for several weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a combined-drug maintenance regimen for chronic/recurrent malaria; includes explicit capsule composition and dosing frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yellow fever transmission essentials and incubation
rubrics_metrics.description: Yellow fever... caused by a special germ or parasite which is communicated to man solely through the agency of the bites of a special mosquito, Stegomyia fasciata... After a person has been bitten by an infected mosquito, from fourteen hours to five days and seventeen hours elapse before the development of the first symptoms--usually this period lasts from three to four days. With the appearance of a single case in a region, a period of two weeks must elapse before the development of another case arising from the first one. This follows because a mosquito, after biting a patient, cannot communicate the germ to another person for twelve days, and two days more must elapse before the disease appears in the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies vector-borne transmission by a particular mosquito species and gives incubation and transmission-timing facts crucial for outbreak control and quarantine timing (i.e., 12-day mosquito development + 2-day onset = ~14-day window).

rubrics_metrics.name: Yellow fever clinical features and prognosis signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Symptoms: chilliness, stomach discomfort, nausea/vomiting, pain through forehead and eyes, flushed and slightly swollen face, bloodshot eyes, whites becoming yellowish in course of thirty-six hours... Temperature ranges from 101 to 103 F, pulse 110–120; pulse usually falls before the temperature does... 'Black vomit' may occur; diminished urine output is an important adverse sign. Mild fever, slight jaundice, and absence of bleeding are favorable signs; black vomit, high fever, and passage of little urine are unfavorable signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes cardinal signs (jaundice, black vomit) and key prognostic markers (urine output, bleeding) to help triage patients and identify severe cases needing urgent care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yellow fever prevention measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Yellow fever... is probably only communicated to man by the bite of a particular kind of mosquito... Spread of the disease is controlled by preventing access of mosquitoes to the bodies of living or dead yellow-fever patients; while personal freedom from yellow fever may be secured by avoiding mosquito bites, through protection by screens indoors, and covering exposed parts of the face, hands, and ankles with oil of pennyroyal or spirit of camphor, while outdoors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes mosquito control (screening, preventing mosquitoes accessing patients or breeding sites) and personal repellents/covering as core preventive actions; historical example (Gorgas) supports efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yellow fever supportive treatment recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is unfortunately no special cure known for yellow fever. The patient should be well covered... give a couple of compound cathartic pills or a tablespoonful of castor oil at the start. Two, or at most three, ten-grain doses of phenacetin at three hours intervals will relieve the pain... Cracked ice... and the application of a mustard paper or paste... will serve to allay vomiting. Cold sponging is the best treatment for fever. The black vomit may be arrested by one-quarter teaspoonful doses of tincture of the chloride of iron... The bowels should be moved daily by injection of warm soapsuds. ...A pint of warm water, containing one-half teaspoonful of salt, should be injected into the bowel night and morning... The diet should consist of milk, diluted with an equal amount of water, broths, gruels... Iced champagne in tablespoonful doses... or two teaspoonful doses of whisky... relieves vomiting and supports the strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific symptomatic and supportive interventions (analgesia, antiemetic measures, cold sponging, iron tincture for black vomit, enemas to stimulate kidneys, dietary restrictions, small alcohol/tonic doses for emesis/support). Emphasizes absence of a curative therapy and reliance on supportive care and complication management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-health demonstration of mosquito-control efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. W. C. Gorgas... during 1901, by ridding Havana of the mosquito carrying the yellow-fever organism through screening barrels and receptacles holding water, and by treating drains, cesspools, etc., with kerosene, succeeded in also eradicating yellow fever from that city, so that in the following year there was not one death from this disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical evidence that environmental mosquito-control measures (screening, oiling breeding sites) can eradicate urban transmission — supports recommended prevention strategies.
